units.title: Foundations & Identity
units.summary: Why you're building, how you see the world, and the core tools of the founder's method.

units.title: Customer & Product
units.summary: From a hunch to a validated product — personas, discovery interviews, MVPs, and the assumptions underneath.

units.title: Marketing & Brand
units.summary: Turning a validated product into a story people hear — segmentation, brand, digital tools, and a real campaign.

units.title: Finance & Operations
units.summary: The numbers and structures that make a business run — unit economics, cash flow, funding, legal, and analytics.

units.title: The Showcase (Capstone)
units.summary: Packaging the year into a brand snapshot and presenting it live at the student showcase.

weeks.title: What Is Entrepreneurship? Mindset, Practice, and Life Design
weeks.question: What does it mean to think like an entrepreneur, and why does it matter?

weeks.title: Finding Your Why: Values, Strengths, and Life Design
weeks.question: What drives you — and how does that connect to the kind of entrepreneur you want to become?

weeks.title: Observing Your World: Walk, Talk, Show Up
weeks.question: What problems are hiding in plain sight — and how do you train yourself to see them?

weeks.title: Business Model Canvas + MVPs + May-B-P
weeks.question: What is the simplest version of your business that you could build right now to test if the problem is real?

weeks.title: AI Basics and Outreach
weeks.question: How do entrepreneurs use AI as a thinking partner and outreach tool — not a shortcut?

weeks.title: Practice Your Pitch: Micro Pitch #1 + Networking Skills
weeks.question: How do you communicate what you do in a way that makes people lean in — not tune out?

weeks.title: Matchmaking + Walk, Talk, Show Up: Deepening Discovery
weeks.question: Who is already doing the work you want to do — and what can you learn from getting close to them?

weeks.title: Creativity + Design Thinking in Action
weeks.question: How do you solve problems you have never seen before — and how do you make sure you are solving the right problem?

weeks.title: Effectuation + Starting with What You Have + Team Building
weeks.question: What can you build right now with what you already have — and who do you need beside you to build it?

weeks.title: Creating Personas + Calculating Total Addressable Market (TAM)
weeks.question: Who exactly is your customer — and how many of them are there?

weeks.title: Customer Discovery Interviews + Target Market Definition
weeks.question: What do your potential customers actually experience — and is it what you assumed?

weeks.title: MVP Building + Testing with Early Users + Vibe Coding
weeks.question: What is the simplest version of your idea you can put in front of a real person this week — and what will you learn when you do?

weeks.title: Choosing the Right Channels + Competitive Research + SWOT Analysis
weeks.question: How do you reach your customer where they already are — and what makes you different from everyone else trying to reach them too?

weeks.title: Sales Strategy: Mapping Processes, People, and Funnels
weeks.question: What does the path from stranger to paying customer actually look like for your business?

weeks.title: Crafting a Compelling Value Proposition + Pricing Models
weeks.question: Why should someone choose you — and what should they pay?

weeks.title: Validating Key Assumptions
weeks.question: Every business runs on assumptions: "People will pay this price." "Customers will find me online." "My supplier can deliver on time." This week students identify the riskiest assumptions in their businesses and test them before they become expensive mistakes.

weeks.title: Reflection + 2-Minute Pitch
weeks.question: This is the Unit 2 final. Students build an 8-slide pitch deck using Notre Dame McCloskey Business Plan Competition Round 2 standards and deliver a 2-minute pitch to the class. This is a real format used in real competitions — hold students to that standard.

weeks.title: Semester 1 Review: Where You Are and Where You Are Going
weeks.question: What have you actually built so far — and what does your business need most in the next 18 weeks?

weeks.title: Customer Segmentation + Messaging
weeks.question: Not everyone is your customer — so who exactly are you talking to, and what do you say to them?

weeks.title: Unique Selling Proposition + Storytelling + Brand Strategy
weeks.question: What makes you different, and how do you tell a story that makes people care?

weeks.title: Digital Marketing Tools
weeks.question: What are the actual tools you use to put your brand in front of your customer — and how do you use them well?

weeks.title: CRM + Outreach Strategies
weeks.question: Once someone shows interest, how do you keep track of them and follow up in a way that actually earns the sale?

weeks.title: AI Campaigns + A/B Testing
weeks.question: How do you use AI to create a full marketing campaign fast — and how do you test which version actually works?

weeks.title: Launch a Real Marketing Campaign
weeks.question: Can you run a real campaign, in the real world, and produce real results this week?

weeks.title: Open House Prep
weeks.question: How do you present your business to the community so they understand it, remember it, and want to support it?

weeks.title: Unit Economics + Revenue Projections
weeks.question: Do you actually make money on each sale — and what happens when you multiply that out?

weeks.title: Cash Flow + Break-Even Analysis
weeks.question: When does the money actually arrive — and how many sales until you stop losing money?

weeks.title: Financial Statements + Budgeting
weeks.question: How do you read the health of a business at a glance — and how do you plan your money before you spend it?

weeks.title: Funding Options + Risk Management
weeks.question: Where does money to grow come from — and how do you protect your business from what could go wrong?

weeks.title: Legal Structures + Operations
weeks.question: How do you make your business official, keep it legal, and run it so it doesn't depend on you remembering everything?

weeks.title: Business Analytics + Data-Driven Decisions
weeks.question: What are the few numbers that actually tell you how your business is doing — and how do you use them to decide?

weeks.title: Team Roles + Operational Planning
weeks.question: Who does what in your business — and how do you plan the work so nothing falls through the cracks?

weeks.title: End of Year Recap
weeks.question: How far have you actually come this year — and how do you tell that story?

weeks.title: The End Part 1: Brand + Business Snapshot
weeks.question: How do you package everything you built this year into one clear, polished picture of your business?

weeks.title: The End Part 2: Showcase Prep
weeks.question: Can you present your business with confidence, handle real questions, and make your booth impossible to walk past?

weeks.title: The End Part 3: Student Showcase
weeks.question: Are you ready to show the world what you built — and to close this year with pride?

skills.name: build-a-skill
skills.description: Help a student write their own Claude skill and send it to RISE staff to be saved. Use when a student wants to make a reusable tool, automate something for their business, or asks what a skill is.

skills.name: business-snapshot
skills.description: Build a one-page Business Snapshot that captures the whole business from a year of work: problem, customer, solution, proof, numbers and what's next. Use for showcase prep, Open House, and Semester reviews.

skills.name: campaign-ab-test
skills.description: Plan a one-week marketing campaign for one customer segment and design a simple A/B test with a clear winner rule. Use when a student is launching a campaign or guessing which message works.

skills.name: discovery-tracker
skills.description: Turn what a student noticed out in the world into Discovery Tracker entries and run the 5 Whys on the strongest one. Use when a student has observations, complaints they overheard, or 'I don't have an idea yet'.

skills.name: interview-script
skills.description: Build a 5-question customer discovery interview that follows The Mom Test, plus a debrief sheet for after. Use when a student needs to talk to real customers or says people 'liked' their idea.

skills.name: may-b-p-test
skills.description: Shrink a business idea into a May-B-P: a version the student can build in 2 weeks with little or no money that tests whether anyone will pay. Use when an idea is too big, or the student doesn't know where to start.

skills.name: micro-pitch
skills.description: Write and tighten a pitch using Problem-Solution-Ask: the 60-second Micro Pitch, plus 30-second and 2-minute versions. Use for pitch practice, networking events, Open House and showcase prep.

skills.name: outreach-message
skills.description: Write a real outreach message, or a 3-message follow-up sequence that adds value instead of nagging. Use when a student needs to reach a customer, mentor, door opener or business owner.

skills.name: persona-and-market
skills.description: Build a customer persona from real evidence and a rough TAM, SAM and SOM with the math shown. Use when a student needs to say who their customer is or how big the market could be.

skills.name: unit-economics
skills.description: Work out the money on one sale (revenue, cost, contribution margin), then the break-even point in units and dollars. Use when a student asks 'will this make money?' or is building projections.

skills.name: value-prop-and-pricing
skills.description: Write a one-sentence value proposition that passes the 'So what?' test, then work out a price three ways: cost-plus, value-based and competitive. Use when a student can't explain why someone would buy, or doesn't know what to charge.
